prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: C#CCN(C)[C@H](C)Cc1ccccc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL2039

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant MAOB
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human MAOB using p-tyramine as substrate after 15 mins by Amplex Red MAO assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.55, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for inhibition of human MAO-B (same target, same organism, confidence score 9), and while the detection methods may differ slightly (Amplex Red fluorometric vs unspecified), the compound (selegiline/rasagiline analog) is a well-characterized irreversible MAO-B inhibitor whose IC50 can be sensitive to pre-incubation time, but the core assay design is sufficiently similar to expect reasonable agreement within 0.3 log units."}
